note: The public fix-log. Weekly triage appends entries here; fix-log.html renders it. Newest first. Keep it honest — an entry stays even when it is embarrassing.

entries.wrong: 134 of the 547 free questions were duplicates — the same question repeated up to 22 times in one bank, padded out to make the counts look bigger. Worse, the copies carried year labels ('2019', '2021') implying they came from real past papers.
entries.fixed: All 134 replaced with genuinely distinct questions across the real syllabus, each with an explanation and a source. The counts are unchanged because the replacements are real questions, not because we quietly shrank the number.

entries.wrong: 292 further questions carried a year label we cannot trace to any paper. Once the duplicates showed those labels were stamped on rather than earned, none of them could be trusted.
entries.fixed: Year labels removed from the free banks entirely. These are practice questions and are now presented as exactly that. Where provenance is real — the NORCET and staff-nurse recall sets — it is still named.

entries.wrong: The answer key said an underwater-seal chest drainage unit is kept at the level of the patient's chest, and the explanation repeated the error by citing the phlebostatic axis.
entries.fixed: Key corrected to below chest level, with an explanation of why gravity drainage and siphon risk decide this. The phlebostatic axis governs haemodynamic transducers, not chest drains.

entries.wrong: Hepatic encephalopathy was keyed to a low-protein diet — teaching that has been withdrawn.
entries.fixed: Key and explanation updated to current AASLD/EASL and ESPEN guidance: maintain protein at roughly 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day. The explanation now names the older teaching so you recognise it in other question banks.

entries.wrong: An autoclave question did not say whether the load was wrapped, which made two options defensible (15 vs 30 minutes).
entries.fixed: Stem now specifies a wrapped load in a gravity-displacement autoclave, and the explanation states both figures and when each applies.

entries.where: Foundations and Medical-Surgical · free topic bank (14 questions)
entries.wrong: Fourteen questions began with "[IMAGE-BASED] The image shows…" but no image was ever displayed, so the question could not be answered as written.
entries.fixed: All fourteen rewritten as self-contained text questions that describe the finding in words.

entries.wrong: The NORCET 9 Mains set reproduced the official paper and was labelled a verbatim replay. Official papers are copyrighted, and the label was wrong on both counts.
entries.fixed: All 121 items rewritten as memory-based recall in our own words, with original per-option explanations and source citations. The official PDF was removed from the site. Every page now labels the set memory-based recall.

entries.wrong: 128 questions carried placeholder explanations such as "Correct option matches standard NORCET teaching" — text that explains nothing.
entries.fixed: All 128 replaced with real explanations that say why the keyed option is right and why the tempting distractor is wrong.

entries.wrong: Questions did not name the reference behind the fact they tested, so a disputed answer could not be checked against anything.
entries.fixed: Every question now carries a source citation at chapter or guideline level, and a validator now fails the build if one is missing.
